item.prompt: [Conversation - Campus security] What does the officer say the depot will not do?
choices: Release a bicycle that is not registered
Release a bicycle without a charge being paid
Hold a bicycle once the rack is repaired
Take in a bicycle whose lock was not cut
item.passage: Transcript: B: My bicycle is gone from the rack outside Kemp Hall. Somebody said security takes them. A: We do, when a rack is being repaired. There was a notice on that one for a week. B: I never saw it. How do I get it back? A: It is in the compound behind the depot. Take the registration sticker number and something with your name on it. B: I do not think I ever registered it. A: Then we register it here first and you collect afterwards. Registration is free, but the depot will not release anything unregistered. B: Is there a fine? A: Not for a rack removal. There is a charge when we cut a lock, and we did not cut one, because yours was not locked. B: It was locked. A: Then what is in the compound is somebody else's bicycle, and that is worth knowing before you walk out there.
item.explanation: The officer says the depot will not release anything unregistered, which is why they register the bicycle at the office before she goes. A charge arises only when security has cut a lock, and he says they cut none here. Nothing is said about the compound emptying when a rack is repaired. Bicycles are taken in from a rack under repair whether or not a lock had to be cut, which is how this one got there.
item.correct_answer: Release a bicycle that is not registered

item.prompt: [Conversation - Language lab] Why has the student not been matched?
choices: The subject she asked for went unfilled this semester
Her request was entered under the wrong language
No native speakers of Spanish enrolled this semester
Her name was left off the open list by mistake
item.passage: Transcript: A: Nothing has happened with my conversation partner. I signed up in September. B: Let me look. You asked for a native speaker of Spanish who is also studying engineering. The second half is the trouble. We match on language first and treat the subject as a preference, and this semester there was no engineer to give you. A: Then I should drop the engineering part. B: You do not have to. I can put you on the open list and leave the preference sitting on your record. A: And in the meantime? B: In the meantime you are matched this week with whoever is free. Most people take that and keep the preference for later. A: Let us do that. B: Done. You will hear from a partner before Friday.
item.explanation: The woman identifies the engineering condition as the obstacle and says there was no engineer to give her this semester. The woman reads the request back correctly as Spanish, so the language on it is not in question. Language is the criterion the lab matches on first, and she offers a partner this week, so speakers were available. An error on the open list is ruled out by the fact that she is only now being put on that list.
item.correct_answer: The subject she asked for went unfilled this semester

item.prompt: [Conversation - Print shop] Why does the man ask for a PDF?
choices: So the type stays where the designer put it
So the file can be enlarged without loss
So the shop can print it at full size
So the poster can go into Thursday's print run
item.passage: Transcript: A: Do you print at A0? I need a conference poster by Friday. B: We do, if the file reaches us by Wednesday noon. A: How is it paid for? B: You pay us, and the department pays you back, since you are presenting. We do not bill them. A: Does it matter what I send? B: A PDF with the fonts embedded. Send the design file and the type will shift when we open it. A: Then get me onto Thursday's run. B: Send the PDF tonight.
item.explanation: His stated reason is that opening a design file makes the type shift, which she will only notice on Friday; embedded fonts prevent that. Enlargement is not what he warns about, and he never suggests detail would be lost. Printing at full size is what the shop does with any file it accepts, and he raises no doubt about it. Thursday's run is the slot he books once he has the file, not the reason for choosing the format.
item.correct_answer: So the type stays where the designer put it

item.prompt: [Conversation - Campus radio] Why has the student's application not reached the meeting?
choices: Her studio training is no longer current
The programming meeting meets monthly
She applied after the list had closed
New hosts get only weekend slots
item.passage: Transcript: B: Three applications for a show, and I have never heard anything back. A: Applications go to the programming meeting, which meets once a month. Have you done the training? B: I did the studio training in the spring. A: That is the one that expires. Anything older than a semester has to be done again before a name goes to the meeting, so your application has been sitting with me. B: Nobody told me that. A: We should have. Do it again on Thursday and I will put you on this month's list myself. B: Would I get a late slot? A: The meeting decides that, not me. New hosts tend to start on weekends, although I have seen exceptions. B: Weekends are fine. A: Thursday, then, and we will see what they say.
item.explanation: The man says training older than a semester must be done again before a name goes to the meeting, and hers was in the spring. The monthly meeting explains how often applications are considered, not why three of hers were never seen. No closing date for the list is mentioned, and he offers to add her to this month's himself. Weekend starts are a tendency in how the meeting assigns slots, which is a later stage than the one she is stuck at.
item.correct_answer: Her studio training is no longer current

item.prompt: [Conversation - Graduation office] What does the man say he can still do about the March order?
choices: Cancel it for a full refund
Move it across to the winter supplier
Hold it open until four weeks before the spring date
Exchange it for the hood the student needs
item.passage: Transcript: A: My confirmation says pick up in May. I ordered the cap and gown back in March. B: That is the standard date. Are you graduating at the winter ceremony? A: I am. B: Then March was the wrong form. The winter order closes in September and those gowns come from another supplier. A: So I have ordered nothing useful. B: You have ordered a spring gown, which I can cancel and refund in full up to four weeks before the spring date, and that has not passed. A: And the winter one? B: Rented on the day. We keep a stock of gowns in the hall. It is the hood that has to be ordered, because the color follows your degree. A: Then let us do the hood now. B: Tell me the degree and I will take the measurement off your record.
item.explanation: He says he can cancel the spring gown and refund it in full, since the four-week point has not passed. The winter gowns come from another supplier, and he never offers to move an order between the two. Four weeks before the spring date is the limit on the refund, not a period he would hold the order open for. The hood is ordered separately at the end of the conversation, as a new order rather than an exchange.
item.correct_answer: Cancel it for a full refund

item.prompt: [Conversation - Study abroad office] What does the adviser say about approval sought after the course is taken?
choices: It comes too late to count toward the major
It is granted once the credits convert cleanly
It takes longer than approval sought in advance
It is settled by the adviser rather than the department
item.passage: Transcript: A: If I take a literature course in Vienna, will it count toward my major here? B: Only when the department signs off before you go. Afterward is too late, and that is the part people get wrong. A: Who signs, you or the department? B: The department. I check that the credits convert, and they decide whether the content counts. A: I have no syllabus yet, only a course title. B: A title will not be enough for them. Send the reading list when it shows up, because that is what they actually read. A: And if it does not show up until August? B: Then it is tight but possible. Send it to me and I will walk it over myself. What does not work is coming home in January with a transcript and asking.
item.explanation: The adviser says the department must sign off before the student goes and that afterward is too late, and she names coming home in January with a transcript as the thing that does not work. Credit conversion is her own check and she never presents it as sufficient on its own. She describes late approval as impossible rather than slow. She is explicit that the department decides whether the content counts, not her.
item.correct_answer: It comes too late to count toward the major
